name: geologic-time-scale

description.en: The geologic time scale in 37 cards: the four eons, the three eras of the Phanerozoic and its twelve periods in order, the era each period belongs to, the current eon, era and period, and when each era began. Front: a prompt such as "Period after the Triassic" or a question such as "Which era does the Jurassic period belong to?"; back: the name in English and Swedish, or an age in millions of years (Ma). Taken from Wikidata and checked against the International Chronostratigraphic Chart (v2026/06), the Geological Survey of Sweden (SGU) and Nationalencyklopedin.
description.sv: Den geologiska tidsskalan i 37 kort: de fyra eonerna, fanerozoikums tre eror och dess tolv perioder i ordning, vilken era varje period hör till, nuvarande eon, era och period samt när varje era började. Framsida: t.ex. ”Perioden efter trias” eller ”Vilken era hör jura till?”; baksida: namnet på engelska och svenska, eller en ålder i miljoner år (Ma). Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata och kontrollerade mot den internationella kronostratigrafiska tabellen (v2026/06), Sveriges geologiska undersökning (SGU) och Nationalencyklopedin.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (a script asserting every name, order and age against the saved ICS chart, NE and SGU texts, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Wikidata (query 1): the items whose English label is one of the four eon names (Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic), the three Phanerozoic era names and the twelve Phanerozoic period names were fetched with their instance of (P31), part of (P361), follows (P155), followed by (P156), start time (P580) and Swedish label. The geological units are the 19 items that are instances of period (Q392928), erathem (Q2464485) or eonothem (Q2669627) and part of the ICS Standard Global Chronostratigraphic (Geochronologic) Scale (Q63463770); the other rows (Wikimedia disambiguation pages and items of other kinds that share an English label, none of them part of Q63463770) were discarded. Query 2 fetched every English, Swedish and multilingual label and alias of the 19 items and of the items they point to; query 3 identified the units before the Cambrian and the Paleozoic (Q188654 Ediacaran, part of Q191935 Neoproterozoic, part of Q104162 Proterozoic). The chains of P155/P156 run unbroken Hadean → Archean → Proterozoic → Phanerozoic, Paleozoic → Mesozoic → Cenozoic and Cambrian → … → Quaternary, and each period is part of (P361) exactly one of the three eras.

2. The International Chronostratigraphic Chart of the International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS): stratigraphy.org/chart is a JavaScript application and returned no content to curl, so the chart's PDF was used. The address pattern https://stratigraphy.org/ICSchart/ChronostratChart<YYYY-MM>.pdf was probed for every month from 2024-12 to 2026-09 (query 5): 2024-12 and 2026-06 exist, and the home page of stratigraphy.org lists "Chart update 2026/06" as its latest chart news, so v2026/06 (dated "(c) International Commission on Stratigraphy, June 2026") is the current version. Both PDFs were downloaded, their text extracted with pypdf and the 2026/06 chart rendered to PNG with PyMuPDF and read (queries 6 and 7). Between v2024/12 and v2026/06 only three stage boundaries changed (259.51 → 259.857, 249.9 → 250.8 and 246.7 → 247.0 Ma); no eon, era or period name, order or base changed.

3. SGU (Sveriges geologiska undersökning, the Swedish geological survey): its page "Sveriges berggrund" (https://www.sgu.se/om-geologi/berg/sveriges-berggrund/) links the brochure "Sveriges berggrund – hur, var och när", whose figure 11 (page 10) names the eons and the Phanerozoic eras in Swedish with the boundaries 541, 252 and 66 million years; the brochure "SGUs tidslinje" (found by a web search restricted to sgu.se) shows a time line whose bands are labelled, from the oldest, HADEIKUM, ARKEIKUM, PROTEROZOIKUM, KAMBRIUM, ORDOVICIUM, SILUR, DEVON, KARBON, PERM, TRIAS, JURA, KRITA, PALEOGEN, NEOGEN and KVARTÄR. Both PDFs were downloaded, their text extracted with pypdf, and the pages with the figure and the time line rendered to PNG and read (queries 8–11), because on the time line's page 3 the band labels are in the image only (the text layer has only page 4's labels).

4. Swedish names: Nationalencyklopedin's article on each of the 19 units was fetched with curl from https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<headword> (ne.py, query 12) and its headword and opening definition extracted (nehead.py, nebody.py). NE writes every name in lower case ("kaʹmbrium", "ordoviʹcium", "siluʹr", "kenozoikum" …), as does SGU in running text ("fram till kambrium", "Under karbon och perm", "tidsperioden kvartär"); SGU's figure and time line set the names as headings in capitals or with an initial capital. The cards use NE's lower-case headwords, which are also the Wikidata sv labels apart from capitalisation (Wikidata gives "Kambrium", "Ordovicium" … with a capital, but "paleogen", "neogen" and "kvartär" in lower case). An attempt to look the names up in SAOL and Svensk ordbok (query 16: sh <scratch>/svenska.sh, which runs curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://svenska.se/tri/f_<saol|so>.php?sok=<word>" for each name) returned only the site's empty page frame (and HTTP 400 for "kvartär"), so svenska.se was not used. NE quotations in the evidence are given as "headword: definition": the headword (and its alternative name, where NE gives one) without NE's stress mark, followed by a colon in place of NE's comma; the definition is verbatim except that the space NE's page puts before some commas is left out; "…" marks an omission and " | " separates quotations from different articles.

5. Cards and cross-check: the cards were written by the script gen.py (query 13) from the saved data; fixgen.py (query 13) revised gen.py once, to write the NE headwords as described in step 4 and to match each quoted fragment against the NE text. Before writing it asserts, for every unit, that the English name is the Wikidata en label and occurs on the ICS chart, that each base age quoted occurs on the chart, that each NE quotation occurs in the saved NE text, that the Swedish name equals the Wikidata sv label apart from the initial capital, that the period-to-era and era-to-eon P361 statements hold, that each successor in the three chains is the P156 of its predecessor and its predecessor the P155 of the successor, and that the SGU labels quoted occur in the SGU text layers (the labels visible only in the rendered images were read from them). Each card has evidence from Wikidata (content), the ICS chart and NE, and, where SGU shows the unit, SGU; the builder's Wikidata checks rerun every order, era and start-time statement and every English label against live Wikidata.

6. Wording: the fronts are the compiler's own ("Period after the Triassic" / "Perioden efter trias", "Which era does the Jurassic period belong to?" / "Vilken era hör jura till?"). The three ages are the ICS base ages rounded to whole millions of years and written as text in no language (zxx), "≈ 66 Ma"; the note gives the chart value as Wikidata also gives it, without the chart's uncertainty. Ma (mega-annum, million years) is the unit of the ICS chart's age column.

7. Notes: every fact in a note is a Wikidata statement or description (query 14–15 and the builder's checks): the start of the Hadean (Q104460 P580, -4567300000, rounded to "about 4567 Ma", which is also the chart's value, and its en description "beginning with the formation of the Earth", given in the note as "as the Earth began to form", not as a formed Earth; query 18), the start times of the eras and the end times of the Permian and the Cretaceous, the two subperiods of the Carboniferous (Q744718, Q373772) and the Tertiary (Q188645, "obsolete term", replaced by the Paleogene and the Neogene). The Swedish "mississippian" and "pennsylvanian" are the English names in lower case, as NE writes them (Wikidata's sv labels "Mississippi" and "Pennsylvania" are not used in Swedish geology texts); "tertiär" is the Wikidata sv label in lower case, as NE writes it.
selection: The four eons (Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic), the three eras of the Phanerozoic (Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic) and its twelve periods (Cambrian to Quaternary), as they stand on the International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2026/06 and in Wikidata. For each chain the deck asks for the first unit and for the unit after each other one, and for the current eon, era and period; for each period it asks for its era; for each era it asks when it began. Left out: the Precambrian eras and periods (Ediacaran, Cryogenian …) and the epochs and ages, which are outside the deck's scope (the eons and the Phanerozoic eras and periods) and would double the deck; the informal "Precambrian" (italic on the ICS chart); the obsolete "Tertiary" (mentioned in a note); the start ages of the periods and of the Precambrian eons, several of which differ between the chart, Wikidata and the Swedish sources (e.g. the Cretaceous, 143.1 ±0.6 Ma on the chart against 145 in Wikidata and SGU and 146 in NE; the Proterozoic, 2500 against NE's 2430); and the proposed Anthropocene, which is not on the chart. Hadean is kept as the first eon: the chart sets it in the Eonothem/Eon column in regular type, and Wikidata and SGU list it as an eon, although NE calls it an informal name. English names are in ICS spelling (Archean, Paleozoic, Cenozoic, not Archaean, Palaeozoic, Caenozoic).

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every name, order, era assignment and age against Wikidata, the ICS chart v2026/06, SGU and NE; the chart version; the Swedish names and their case.
rounds.scope: All cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: Wikidata, the ICS chart, SGU and NE agree on every name, every order and every period's era. The Swedish names agree in spelling everywhere; Wikidata capitalises 16 of the 19 sv labels where NE and SGU's running text write lower case. Wikidata's start times differ from the current chart for some periods (not on any card); the start of the Paleozoic differs between the current chart and older sources, which the note on that card states. No Wikidata check was skipped except the sv label checks on the 16 capitalised labels.

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish labels are capitalised for 16 units ("Hadeikum", "Arkeikum", "Proterozoikum", "Fanerozoikum", "Paleozoikum", "Mesozoikum", "Kenozoikum", "Kambrium", "Ordovicium", "Silur", "Devon", "Karbon", "Perm", "Trias", "Jura", "Krita") but lower case for "paleogen", "neogen" and "kvartär". NE's headwords are all lower case ("kaʹmbrium", "kenozoikum" …), and SGU writes "fram till kambrium", "Under karbon och perm", "tidsperioden kvartär" in running text, though its figures set the names as headings.
findings.resolution: The Swedish backs are the lower-case forms, as in NE and in Swedish running text, consistently across the deck. The builder checks the sv label only for paleogen, neogen and kvartär, where it is the same text; for the other 16 the case-sensitive check would compare a different capitalisation, so the Swedish name is verified by NE and SGU in the evidence and by gen.py (sv label equal apart from the initial capital).

findings.issue: The start of the Paleozoic (and of the Phanerozoic and the Cambrian) is 538.8 ±0.6 Ma on the ICS chart v2026/06 and v2024/12 and in Wikidata, but 541 in SGU's figure ("Sveriges berggrund – hur, var och när"), 542 in SGU's time line and in NE, values from older charts.
findings.resolution: The card follows the current chart and Wikidata ("≈ 539 Ma") and its note says that older charts and books give 541 or 542 Ma.

findings.issue: The start of the Mesozoic is 251.902 ±0.024 Ma on the chart and in Wikidata, 252 in SGU's figure, 251 in SGU's time line and NE ("ca 251–66").
findings.resolution: "≈ 252 Ma" is the chart value rounded to whole millions; the exact value is in the note. The 251 of the older sources is the same boundary given less precisely (rounded down).

findings.issue: SGU's time line gives 65 million years for the start of the Paleogene (and so the Cenozoic); the chart, Wikidata, SGU's figure and NE give 66.
findings.resolution: The card follows the chart: "≈ 66 Ma".

findings.issue: Wikidata's start times of several periods differ from the current chart: Cretaceous 145 Ma (chart 143.1 ±0.6, already so in v2024/12; SGU 145, NE 146), Neogene 23.03 (chart 23.04), Devonian 419.2 (chart 419.62 ±1.36), Carboniferous 358.9 (chart 358.86 ±0.19), Hadean 4567.3 (chart 4567).
findings.resolution: No card gives these ages; the deck asks only for the start of the three eras, where Wikidata and the chart agree (66, 251.902, 538.8). Recorded so that a later edit of the deck does not take period ages from Wikidata unchecked.

findings.issue: NE calls the Hadean "informellt namn på de första 537 miljoner åren av jordens historia", while the ICS chart sets "Hadean" in the Eonothem/Eon column in regular type (informal units are italic, such as "Precambrian") and Wikidata and SGU treat it as an eon.
findings.resolution: Kept as the first eon, following the chart; NE's description is quoted in the card's evidence.

findings.issue: In North America the Carboniferous is often divided into two periods, the Mississippian and the Pennsylvanian (NE: "I Nordamerika motsvaras karbon av två perioder"); the ICS chart shows them as subsystems of the Carboniferous. A North American learner might answer "Mississippian".
findings.resolution: The card answers with the international period, Carboniferous, and its note names the North American division.

findings.issue: Older books name the period after the Cretaceous "Tertiary" (Paleogene and Neogene together); NE calls tertiär "en av den Internationella stratigrafiska kommissionen numera ej rekommenderad beteckning", and it is not on the ICS chart.
findings.resolution: The cards answer Paleogene and Neogene, as the chart does; their notes mention the former name.

findings.issue: The text layer of SGU's figure 11 reads "Hadeaikum"; the brochure's own body text ("kallade Hadeikum och Arkeikum"), SGU's time line ("HADEIKUM"), NE and Wikidata write hadeikum.
findings.resolution: A misprint in that figure; the card uses hadeikum.

findings.issue: Version check: the ICS chart was v2024/12 according to a web search, but the PDF address for v2026/06 exists and stratigraphy.org's latest news is "Chart update 2026/06". The text of the two versions differs only in three stage ages (Wuchiapingian 259.51 → 259.857, Olenekian 249.9 → 250.8, Anisian 246.7 → 247.0 Ma) and the citation.
findings.resolution: The deck cites v2026/06; nothing on a card changed between the versions. The Quaternary remains the current period on the chart (the proposed Anthropocene is not on it).

findings.issue: The start of the Proterozoic is 2500 Ma on the chart and in Wikidata and SGU, but 2 430 in NE.
findings.resolution: No card gives the start of a Precambrian eon; the order, on which all sources agree, is what the card asks.

rounds.scope: All 37 cards, against live Wikidata (labels, P361, P155, P156, P580 of the 19 units) and the ICS chart v2026/06 (downloaded, text-extracted and its fonts inspected); the chart version; the notes.
rounds.summary: Every order, every period's era and the three era base ages match the chart and Wikidata, all Wikidata checks hold live, v2026/06 is the newest chart and the Quaternary is still the current period. One warning: the Hadean note equated 4567 Ma with the Earth's formation, which is the age of the Solar System's oldest solids (USGS gives the Earth's age as 4.54 billion years). Fixed.

findings.issue: The note "Began with the formation of the Earth, ≈ 4567 Ma" ties 4567 Ma to the Earth's formation; that value is the chart's base of the Hadean and the age of the oldest solid matter in the Solar System (NE: "den initiala sammansmältningen av fast materia"), while the Earth's age is usually given as about 4540 Ma.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: NE in the card's own evidence dates the start to the first solid matter, not to a formed Earth. Wikidata's own description of Q104460 ("beginning with the formation of the Earth about 4.567 billion years ago", query 15) makes the same equation, so it was not followed. The note now reads "Starts about 4567 Ma (ICS chart), as the Earth began to form" / "Börjar för ca 4 567 miljoner år sedan (ICS-tabellen), när jorden började bildas", which no longer equates the date with a formed Earth.

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent language, translation and language tags reviewer
rounds.scope: All 37 cards, the title, the description and the keywords: language tags, Swedish names and idiom, English wording, typography.
rounds.summary: Every text is correctly tagged and the Swedish names follow NE's lower-case forms consistently. One warning (title case in the English title) and five suggestions; the title, the description, the twelve era fronts, the Hadean and Carboniferous notes and the number spacing were changed; the article before "Earth" was left as it was.

findings.issue: The English title "Geologic Time Scale" is in title case, where the other authored decks use sentence case.
findings.resolution: Title changed to "Geologic time scale".

findings.issue: The description calls the fronts "a question such as \"Period after the Triassic\"", which is a prompt, not a question.
findings.resolution: English: "Front: a prompt such as \"Period after the Triassic\" or a question such as \"Which era does the Jurassic period belong to?\"". Swedish: "Framsida: t.ex. ”Perioden efter trias” eller ”Vilken era hör jura till?”" (the suggested "uppmaning" means an exhortation in Swedish, which these fronts are not).

findings.issue: The twelve English fronts "The <X> period belongs to which era?" use a quiz-show word order; also ordovician-era … quaternary-era.
findings.resolution: All twelve now read "Which era does the <X> period belong to?"; the examples in the description and in method step 6 were updated.

findings.issue: "Earth's history" on the front but "the formation of the Earth" in the note; "≈" in Swedish running prose where Swedish writes "ca".
findings.resolution: The Swedish note now says "för ca 4 567 miljoner år sedan" (rewritten in round 1). The article was kept: "Earth's history" and "the Earth" are both standard English and the round-1 wording ("as the Earth began to form") reads naturally with it.

findings.issue: The appositive "…, subperiods on the ICS chart" / "…, underperioder i ICS-tabellen" is loose.
findings.resolution: The note was rewritten (see round 3, which also required it to rest on Wikidata): "Divided into two subperiods, the Mississippian (older) and the Pennsylvanian" / "Indelas i två underperioder, mississippian (äldre) och pennsylvanian". The lower-case Swedish forms are kept, as the reviewer agreed.

findings.issue: Numbers and units are separated by ordinary spaces ("4 567", "538,8 ± 0,6 miljoner år"), which can break across lines; Språkrådet recommends a non-breaking space. Also mesozoic-start, cenozoic-start and first-eon.
findings.resolution: Non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) are now used in "4 567" and between each number and "Ma" / "miljoner" in the four notes, and in the three backs ("≈ 539 Ma" …). The ± values were removed in round 3.

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer
rounds.scope: The sources and their licence pages, the licensing paragraph, the method, the queries and every card's evidence; spot checks against freshly fetched sources.
rounds.summary: The CC0 licence holds and all three closed sources are verification only, but some notes carried facts that only verification sources gave; they were rewritten to rest on Wikidata statements and descriptions (new evidence and 15 new checks), and the licensing paragraph now says so and names the right of quotation. The NE tertiär locator, the missing svenska.sh and fixgen.py commands, the NE quotation convention, the SGU figure caption and misprint, the NE article URLs and the deck's own script check in the "Who did the work" paragraph were all corrected.

findings.issue: Facts on the cards came only from verification sources: the ± uncertainties (paleozoic-start, mesozoic-start), "older charts and books give 541 or 542 Ma" (paleozoic-start), the Mississippian/Pennsylvanian note (period-after-devonian) and "a name no longer recommended" for the Tertiary; the licensing paragraph claimed verification sources only confirmed Wikidata's facts.
findings.resolution: Confirmed against live Wikidata (queries 14–15): the P580 statements of the Paleozoic, the Cambrian and the Phanerozoic carry no uncertainty and no other value (no 541 or 542), so the ± values and the 541/542 remark were removed; the age notes now give the value Wikidata and the chart share, and "also the start of the Phanerozoic and the Cambrian" and "the end of the Permian / the Cretaceous" rest on new P580 and P582 checks. The Carboniferous note now says only what Q744718 and Q373772 give (two subperiods, part of the Carboniferous, the Mississippian first), with new evidence and checks; the North American usage, which only NE gave, was dropped. The Tertiary notes now say "an obsolete term", Wikidata's description of Q188645, with new evidence and checks on its en label and its P1366 (replaced by) Paleogene and Neogene. The licensing paragraph and the ICS chart's usedFor were reworded, and method step 7 lists where each note's facts come from.

findings.issue: The NE "tertiär" locator says its summary appears on the paleogen and neogen articles, but it appears only on the neogen page, and "tertiär" is missing from the NE source title. Also period-after-paleogene.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: "rekommenderad" occurs twice in the saved ne-neogen.html and not at all in ne-paleogen.html. The locator now reads "article \"tertiär\" (its summary shown on the neogen article page, https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/neogen)" on both cards, and "tertiär" was added to the NE source title.

findings.issue: svenska.sh (the svenska.se lookup) and fixgen.py (which rewrote gen.py) were run but are not recorded under queries.
findings.resolution: Confirmed. Query 16 records svenska.sh with its loop verbatim and its outcome; query 13 now lists fixgen.py before gen.py and says what it changed; method step 5 mentions it.

findings.issue: The NE "says" texts are presented as quotations, but the headword punctuation was changed ("hadeʹikum, hadeiska tiden , informellt namn" became "hadeikum, hadeiska tiden: informellt namn").
findings.resolution: Confirmed in fixgen.py and the saved NE pages. Method step 4 now states the convention once: "headword: definition", the headword without NE's stress mark and with a colon in place of NE's comma, the definition verbatim except for the space NE's page puts before some commas, "…" for omissions and " | " between articles.

findings.issue: The NE quotations are justified with NE's own permission, which covers non-commercial quotation only; the legal basis for quoting them in the published report is not named.
findings.resolution: The licensing paragraph now says the short NE and SGU quotations in the evidence are quoted under the right of quotation (upphovsrättslagen 22 §) with the source named and are not part of the deck. The quotations were not shortened: each is the opening definition that proves the fact on the card.

findings.issue: The SGU figure is described imprecisely: the printed figure itself reads "Hadeaikum" (not only the text layer), and its caption is "Jordens tidsåldrar och utveckling", not "Jordens tidsåldrar" (the section heading).
findings.resolution: Confirmed: a 200 dpi rendering of the figure (query 17) shows the printed label "Hadeaikum", and the text layer has "Figur 11. Jordens tidsåldrar och utveckling, åldrar i miljoner år." The sgu-berggrund evidence (eon-after-proterozoic, current-eon) now reads 'figure 11 ("Jordens tidsåldrar och utveckling") … Hadeikum (printed "Hadeaikum")', and the source's usedFor gives the caption and the misprint. The round-0 finding is kept as recorded; this entry corrects it. first-eon cites only the SGU time line, which reads HADEIKUM, so its evidence did not change for this finding.

findings.issue: The NE source URL is the encyclopedia's index page, and some locators say "articles" for a single article.
findings.resolution: The NE source's usedFor and method step 4 now give the article address pattern https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<headword>; every locator that names one article now says "article".

findings.issue: The "Who did the work" paragraph names no deck-specific check, although gen.py asserts every name, order, era, age and quotation against the saved sources.
findings.resolution: The parenthesis now reads "(a script asserting every name, order and age against the saved ICS chart, NE and SGU texts, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators)".

rounds.lens: Re-check of changed cards and a sample (facts, language, documentation)
rounds.scope: The 24 cards changed in round 3 and every third card (32 cards), the metadata, the licence and the documentation; every Wikidata check against live wbgetentities, the ICS chart v2026/06, the NE and SGU quotations.
rounds.summary: Nothing wrong or misleading; all checks hold live, v2026/06 is still the newest chart, quotations are verbatim and the builds match the dossier. Three documentation suggestions were applied: the source of the Hadean note, a mark where an NE quotation breaks off, and a published reason for leaving out the Precambrian subdivisions, epochs and ages.

findings.issue: Method step 7 does not say what the Hadean note "Starts about 4567 Ma (ICS chart), as the Earth began to form" rests on; it credits only the ICS chart, a verification source, and "as the Earth began to form" is a looser form of Wikidata's description that round 1 said was not followed.
findings.resolution: Confirmed with a fresh wbgetentities call (query 18): Q104460 P580 is -4567300000 and its en description is "… beginning with the formation of the Earth about 4.567 billion years ago". Round 1 declined the equation of 4567 Ma with a formed Earth, not the description's "beginning with the formation", which the note follows. Method step 7 now names the Hadean's P580 and description; the note's attribution reads "(ICS chart, Wikidata)" / "(ICS-tabellen, Wikidata)", and the card's Wikidata evidence quotes the description.

findings.issue: The NE "karbon" quotation breaks off mid-parenthesis without a mark, and since round 3 dropped the North American usage it is unclear what it supports.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: the quotation is verbatim up to where NE's public text ends. It now ends with "…" and the note "(the public text ends here; quoted for NE's lower-case forms mississippian and pennsylvanian)".

findings.issue: The selection gives "the brief did not ask for" as a reason for leaving out the Precambrian eras and periods and the epochs and ages, but the brief is not published.
findings.resolution: The selection now states the criterion: they "are outside the deck's scope (the eons and the Phanerozoic eras and periods) and would double the deck".

rounds.scope: All 37 cards, the title, description, keywords and notes; names, order, era assignments and era base ages against the ICS chart v2026/06 and live Wikidata; the Swedish text and the language tags.
rounds.summary: No errors or warnings. Two optional wording suggestions were applied: the English fronts of the three "current" cards now say "geologic", so "The current era" cannot be read as the Common Era, and the English keyword "geological periods" became "geologic periods" to match the rest of the deck.

findings.issue: In English, "The current era" is also a set phrase for the Common Era (CE); the front reads less cleanly than it could.
findings.resolution: Accepted. The English front now reads "The current geologic era", and current-eon and current-period were changed the same way ("The current geologic eon", "The current geologic period") for consistency. The Swedish fronts ("Den nuvarande eran" …) were kept: in Swedish the Common Era is "vår tideräkning", so they are not ambiguous. The answers and evidence are unchanged.

findings.issue: The English keywords mix "geologic" and "geological" ("geologic time scale" next to "geological periods"), while the title and cards use "geologic".
findings.resolution: Accepted: the keyword is now "geologic periods". The Swedish keyword "geologiska perioder" is unaffected (Swedish has one form).
